bugs: Minor: a job still waiting in the queue after CLAIM_MINUTES (60) is queued a second time, and the command still reports 'Queued 1' (probe: 2 rows in jobs). The handle() guard stops a second CRM call (probe: 1 HTTP call), so the harm is limited to extra queue entries.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:42-45: catches, updates and rethrows instead of recording the final error in failed(). It also drops the existing Log::error, which changes observable behaviour.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:23: a closure is used as a query-builder factory ($pending()). It works, but a named local scope would be clearer.

app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:9-10: #[Signature]/#[Description] attributes are added to one command while NormalizeSubscriberEmails still uses properties. That is unrelated churn and leaves the two commands inconsistent.
strengths: Finds all four root causes: the swallowed exception, re-dispatch that ignores crm_sync_queued_at, withoutOverlapping() with the default 24h mutex, and chunk() paging over the column it updates.

Treats the duplicate-CRM-call problem as a layered fix: an atomic conditional-UPDATE claim, a stale-claim TTL, and an idempotency guard in handle() that a probe confirmed (one CRM call when duplicate jobs exist).
WithoutOverlapping uses ->dontRelease()->expireAfter(60), so a killed worker cannot hold the per-job lock forever and contending duplicates do not burn tries.
Uses current Laravel 13 queue attributes (#[Tries], #[Backoff], #[Timeout]); confirmed present in vendor.

Strongest tests: they run real queue:work attempts, check Http::assertSentCount(3), failed_jobs and the jobs table, and test the stale claim using the CLAIM_MINUTES constant rather than a magic number.
A probe confirmed that a failed subscriber is re-dispatched after the claim TTL and does reach the CRM.

bugs: handle() has no idempotency guard. If a duplicate job exists, for example because the queue backlog outlasted uniqueFor=3600 or a dispatch happened outside the command, the CRM is called again for an already-synced subscriber (probe: 2 CRM calls). Symptom 2 is about exactly this backed-up-queue situation.

The requeue window (15 min) does not match uniqueFor (60 min). Between them the command bumps crm_sync_queued_at and reports 'Queued N' while ShouldBeUnique silently drops the dispatch, so the reported count is misleading.
antipatterns: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:43-47: try/catch/rethrow instead of a failed() hook for the final error state.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:22-30: the claim is read and then updated without a conditional UPDATE. This is acceptable only because the schedule uses withoutOverlapping.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:80: travel(61) is tied to uniqueFor, not to REQUEUE_AFTER_MINUTES, so the requeue boundary (15 min) is never tested.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:101: the schedule test only checks the expiresAt property (the same is true of the other two implementations).
strengths: The smallest diff. Each of the four root causes is fixed directly: rethrow plus backoff/timeout, a crm_sync_queued_at filter plus ShouldBeUnique, withoutOverlapping(10), and chunkById.
Good worker-driven failed_jobs test, plus a test that only one database job is pushed per subscriber.
A probe confirmed that a failed subscriber is re-dispatched later and reaches the CRM.

bugs: The claim TTL (30 min) does not match uniqueFor (3600 s). After 30 min a still-pending job is 'claimed' again and counted as queued, but ShouldBeUnique drops the dispatch, so the 'Queued N' output is misleading. The handle() guard means there is no duplicate CRM call.
crm_last_error is now written only in failed(), so errors from intermediate attempts are not recorded, and the existing Log::error was removed. This is a small change in behaviour.
antipatterns: Uses ShouldBeUnique, an atomic claim and an in-handle guard all together. Three overlapping de-duplication mechanisms, two of them with different TTLs, is somewhat belt-and-braces.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:51: calls failed() by hand with a made-up exception instead of checking the result of a real worker run.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:64-67: the queue:work result is not asserted, and available_at is changed directly in the database instead of using time travel.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:3-8: the use statements are not sorted (Console comes after Foundation).
strengths: The most idiomatic Eloquent: a #[Scope] local scope (needsCrmSync), reused for both the lazyById read and the atomic conditional UPDATE claim.
Records the terminal error in a proper failed() hook and removes the swallowing try/catch completely.
lazyById()->each() fixes the normalize command cleanly.
Its idempotency guard prevents a duplicate CRM call (probe confirmed), and a failed subscriber is re-dispatched after the TTL (probe confirmed).
The stale-claim test covers both sides of the TTL boundary.

v.rationale: All three implementations pass their own suites (impl-2: 11 tests, impl-3: 12, impl-1: 12). All three found the same four root causes: the try/catch that swallowed exceptions so jobs never failed; dispatch-sync re-queuing every unsynced subscriber every minute because it never checked crm_sync_queued_at; Schedule::withoutOverlapping() using the default 24-hour mutex expiry; and chunk() paging over the email_normalized column it was updating. Probes run against each: a full worker failure followed by a later scheduler re-dispatch that succeeds (all pass); a stale duplicate job running after the subscriber is synced; a job still pending past the claim TTL; and normalising a mix of normalised and unnormalised rows (all pass). The duplicate-job probe is what separates them. impl-2 has no idempotency guard and calls the CRM twice, while impl-1 and impl-3 call it once. impl-2 and impl-3 also use claim windows that differ from uniqueFor, so the command's 'Queued' count can be wrong. impl-1 ranks first: it has the most complete fix (atomic claim, handle guard, and a WithoutOverlapping job lock that expires), the most modern Laravel 13 idioms (queue attributes, all verified in vendor), and the strongest tests based on real worker runs. Its weaknesses are a builder closure where a scope would be clearer, try/catch/rethrow instead of failed(), and unrelated attribute churn. impl-3 is close behind, with better Eloquent (a #[Scope] and a failed() hook) but some redundant de-duplication layers and weaker failure-path tests. impl-2 is the simplest but leaves the duplicate CRM call possible, the backed-up-queue case that symptom 2 describes.
